## Process lifecycle

- Run long-lived servers and watchers in a persistent session such as tmux.
- Do not background them in bounded commands without explicit detachment and cleanup.
- After a timeout, inspect the process and endpoint before retrying or claiming failure.

## Linux browser and WebGPU capture

- Use the preinstalled `playwright-cli` executable from Actions or SSH.
- Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
- Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
- Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
- Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.
- Inspect the image. Reject loading screens, empty grids, and blank canvases.
- Report SwiftShader as CPU software rendering. Do not claim GPU hardware acceleration.
- Inspect `$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json` for launch settings.
- Use `playwright-cli --help` for commands and named sessions. Pass configuration only to `open`.

## Mobile browser games

- Support Android and iOS phones and tablets with responsive layouts and usable touch controls.
- Keep gameplay and controls visible within safe areas and avoid browser gesture conflicts.
- Add tilt controls only when appropriate; offer touch alternatives and request iOS motion permission from a user gesture when needed.
- Follow explicit device and control requirements in the user request.

# OMG (Oh My GitHub) agent instructions

Do not implement, suggest, report, or propose security issues unless the user explicitly asks for a security review.
Inspect the OpenCode implementation at `/Users/igor/Documents/ChatGPT/opencode` and [anomalyco/opencode](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode) for related requests.

## Wiki index

- [OpenCode workflow](wiki/opencode.md)
- [Test OpenCode execution](wiki/opencode-v2-experiment.md)
- [Oh My Github App](https://github.com/denaidark/omsite/blob/main/wiki/oh-my-github-app.md)
- [Temporary Mac SSH access](wiki/access.md)
- [Testing and verification](wiki/testing.md)
- [OmGithub publishing](https://github.com/denaidark/omsite/blob/main/wiki/omgithub.md)


## Main project file

The main project file is [.github/workflows/opencode.yml](.github/workflows/opencode.yml).

Keep the local [game issue E2E skill](.agents/skills/game-issue-e2e/SKILL.md)
aligned with this workflow. Create an issue with `OpenCode` and only user-requested mode labels already attached, to start the native `issues.opened` listener. Wait only for the
initial OpenCode session link during E2E kickoff. Install the listener on the
default branch before requesting execution. Validate author access and freeze
the request inside Actions before starting the reusable execution job.
Set repository variable `OPENCODE_ACCESS=everyone` to accept any issue author
for labeled issues. Keep the App as a setup
helper. Use Actions concurrency to serialize each issue.
Store `branch` in an `omgithub-request:v1` JSON HTML comment to select the
project checkout, result base, and workflow. Let default-branch preparation
dispatch the selected branch. Run preparation and OpenCode in that branch run.

## Shell timing

When writing shell scripts,
always add explicit per-command execution-time measurements between commands.
Use `/usr/bin/time -p` or a small timing helper around each meaningful command;
the outer command duration is not sufficient because it hides which step is
slow or hung. Use `/usr/bin/time` only in scripts; do not invoke it directly in
interactive shell commands.

## Ideas

Store durable implementation ideas as individual Markdown files under
`./ideas/`, using descriptive kebab-case filenames such as
`ideas/opencode-oauth-env-auth.md`.




## Links in handoffs

When a relevant URL or stable identifier exists, include a clickable Markdown
link in the user-facing response. Link GitHub issues, Actions runs, pull
requests, commits, releases, public app URLs, and Codex tasks/threads rather
than reporting only their numbers or plain text. For Codex tasks/threads, use
the `codex://threads/<thread-id>` URL format.

When mentioning a commit, append its relative age in hours or days.

## OpenCode GitHub Actions

To execute an issue, create it with `OpenCode` and only mode labels explicitly requested by the user.
Check for a native `issues` run and successful preparation.
The workflow starts a temporary AgentsWeb SSH session,
verifies it, runs OpenCode, and cleans up the SSH session afterward.

When monitoring a triggered run, use `gh run watch <run-id> --repo denaidark/OhMyGithub --exit-status` for overall job status.
Do not use `gh run view --log` to read logs from a running task: GitHub reports that
logs are unavailable until completion. Use `bash scripts/ssh-run-log.sh <run-id>`
for the live Actions log over SSH. Do not use tight `for` loops around `gh run list`,
which needlessly consume GitHub API rate limit.

Free OpenCode models are limited per egress IP, not per account.
Treat a local `FreeUsageLimitError` 429 as local only.
Read the runner's own `Selected model` and provider errors before blaming quota.
Use `retryAfterMs` as the reset bound.
Run repeated V2 tests with a connected provider; do not spend the free allowance on retries.

Interrupting a V2 turn before the assistant message projects leaves no stopped message to save.
Wait for that assistant message before requiring the interrupted idle marker.

To connect to an issue's live worker, find its run ID with
`gh run list --repo denaidark/OhMyGithub --workflow opencode.yml --status in_progress`,
then run `bash scripts/ssh-run-log.sh <run-id>` to discover the host and port and SSH
with `~/.ssh/aiplay-agentsweb` as shown by the helper.

When the user asks to check a live OpenCode workflow, always pull the runner logs
over SSH first, using `scripts/ssh-run-log.sh` or a targeted SSH read from the
same runner. Base the answer on those logs before discussing whether an action
is confirmed; do not lead with a generic inability-to-confirm statement when
live log evidence can be collected.

For real-time inspection from a live temporary SSH session, use the helper:

```sh
bash scripts/ssh-run-log.sh <run-id>
```

The helper discovers the temporary SSH command from the triggering issue or pull
request, then follows the freshest `_diag/pages` log. The runner uploads chunks from
`_diag/blocks` to GitHub. Do not print environment files, tokens, or private keys while
inspecting the runner.

## Mac SSH access

The Mac private key stays at `~/.ssh/aiplay-agentsweb`. Its public key is
stored in the repository Actions secret `AGENTSWEB_SSH_PUBLIC_KEY`. The issue
commented by the workflow contains a directly usable command such as:

```sh
ssh -i ~/.ssh/aiplay-agentsweb -p <port> runner@<run-name>.agentsweb.space
```

The command works only while the corresponding Actions job is running.

## Connecting to a live OpenCode worker

Use the repository helper to discover the worker host and port from the broker
or issue comment. It uses the persistent local key `~/.ssh/aiplay-agentsweb`:

```sh
bash scripts/ssh-run-log.sh <run-id> --repo denaidark/OhMyGithub
```

For an interactive shell, reuse the host and port printed by the helper and
use the same key:

```sh
ssh -tt -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no \
  -o UserKnownHostsFile=/dev/null \
  -i ~/.ssh/aiplay-agentsweb \
  -p <port> runner@<run-name>.agentsweb.space
```

Do not substitute the generated runner key under `sshworker/outputs/keys/`; it
can produce a misleading `Permission denied (publickey)` result. Temporary
worker SSH access ends when the Actions job and session are cleaned up. Never
print secrets while inspecting a worker.

import { existsSync, readFileSync, writeFileSync, mkdirSync, statSync } from 'node:fs'
import { resolve, join, extname } from 'node:path'
import { createHash } from 'node:crypto'
import { createServer } from 'node:http'
import { spawn } from 'node:child_process'
import { pathToFileURL } from 'node:url'
import { child } from './session-lifecycle.mjs'
import { livePreviewScript, watchProject } from './live-preview.mjs'

export function projectType(root) {
  if (existsSync(join(root, 'package.json'))) {
    const p = JSON.parse(readFileSync(join(root, 'package.json'), 'utf8'))
    if (p.dependencies?.next || p.devDependencies?.next) throw new Error('Unsupported framework: customize start.sh and provide static deployment output.')
    if (p.dependencies?.vite || p.devDependencies?.vite) return 'vite'
    throw new Error('Unsupported package project: customize start.sh and deployment output.')
  }
  if (existsSync(join(root, 'index.html'))) return 'html'
  throw new Error('No generated index.html or supported package project.')
}
export async function start(root = process.cwd()) {
  const type = projectType(root)
  const projectRoot = resolve(root)
  if (type === 'vite') {
    const stampDir = process.env.OPENCODE_WEB_DIR || join(root, 'node_modules', '.cache')
    mkdirSync(stampDir, { recursive: true })
    const stamp = join(stampDir, 'default-dependencies')
    const lock = join(root, 'package-lock.json')
    const hash = createHash('sha256').update(readFileSync(join(root, 'package.json'))).update(existsSync(lock) ? readFileSync(lock) : '').digest('hex')
    let old = ''
    try { old = readFileSync(stamp, 'utf8') } catch {}
    if (old !== hash || !existsSync(join(root, 'node_modules/vite'))) {
      await child('npm', [existsSync(lock) ? 'ci' : 'install', '--no-audit', '--no-fund'], { cwd: root })
      mkdirSync(stampDir, { recursive: true })
      const installedHash = createHash('sha256').update(readFileSync(join(root, 'package.json'))).update(existsSync(lock) ? readFileSync(lock) : '').digest('hex')
      writeFileSync(stamp, installedHash)
    }
    await child(process.execPath, [join(root, 'node_modules/vite/bin/vite.js'), 'build', '--base', './'], { cwd: root })
    root = join(root, 'dist')
  }
  if (!existsSync(join(root, 'index.html'))) throw new Error('Static deployment output must contain index.html.')
  if (process.env.OPENCODE_WEB_DIR) writeFileSync(join(process.env.OPENCODE_WEB_DIR, 'deployment-output.json'), JSON.stringify({ project: projectRoot, directory: resolve(root) }))
  const mime = { '.html':'text/html', '.js':'application/javascript', '.css':'text/css', '.json':'application/json', '.svg':'image/svg+xml', '.png':'image/png', '.jpg':'image/jpeg', '.webp':'image/webp', '.wasm':'application/wasm', '.glb':'model/gltf-binary' }
  const clients = new Set()
  const stopWatching = watchProject(root, () => { for (const client of clients) client.write('event: change\ndata: changed\n\n') })
  const keepAlive = setInterval(() => { for (const client of clients) client.write(': keepalive\n\n') }, 20000)
  const buildWatcher = type === 'vite' ? spawn(process.execPath, [join(projectRoot, 'node_modules/vite/bin/vite.js'), 'build', '--base', './', '--watch'], { cwd: projectRoot, stdio: 'inherit' }) : null
  const server = createServer((req, res) => {
    try {
      const url = new URL(req.url, 'http://localhost')
      if (url.pathname === '/__omgithub/live') {
        res.writeHead(200, { 'Content-Type': 'text/event-stream', 'Cache-Control': 'no-cache', 'X-Accel-Buffering': 'no', Connection: 'keep-alive' })
        res.write(': connected\n\n')
        clients.add(res)
        req.on('close', () => clients.delete(res))
        return
      }
      const path = resolve(root, '.' + decodeURIComponent(url.pathname))
      if (path !== resolve(root) && !path.startsWith(resolve(root) + '/')) { res.writeHead(404); res.end(); return }
      const file = statSync(path).isDirectory() ? join(path, 'index.html') : path
      res.setHeader('Content-Type', mime[extname(file)] || 'application/octet-stream')
      res.setHeader('Cache-Control', url.searchParams.has('omgithub_live') ? 'no-store' : 'no-cache')
      const content = readFileSync(file)
      if (extname(file) === '.html' && url.searchParams.get('omgithub_live') === '1') {
        const html = content.toString()
        res.end(/<\/body\s*>/i.test(html) ? html.replace(/<\/body\s*>/i, `${livePreviewScript}</body>`) : html + livePreviewScript)
      } else res.end(content)
    } catch { res.writeHead(404); res.end('Not found') }
  })
  server.on('close', () => { stopWatching(); clearInterval(keepAlive); buildWatcher?.kill(); for (const client of clients) client.end() })
  server.listen(Number(process.env.PORT || 3000), '0.0.0.0')
  return server
}
if (process.argv[1] && import.meta.url === pathToFileURL(process.argv[1]).href) await start()

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Build a complete, playable 3D creature collector adventure game in Three.js with 8 regions, gyms, leveling, turn-based battles, crafting/scavenging treats, trainer customization, and original monster-sized creatures.

## Requirements
- 8 explorable regions and competitive gyms.
- Fun leveling system.
- Capture via battling and treats crafted from scavenged materials.
- Male/female trainer customization.
- Original creature designs, Monster Hunter-sized but can be cute.
- Turn-based Pokémon-style battle system.
- Build immediately without clarifying questions; note assumptions only at completion.

## Decisions
- Use Vite + Three.js with procedural geometry/canvas textures; no external art assets.
- Title `TITANBOUND`, 8 themed regions, 19 creatures, 8 gym leaders/sigils.
- Real-time third-person exploration + separate turn-based battle arena.
- Procedural low-poly art with bloom, fog, gradient skies, particles, and shadows.
- Persist progress in `localStorage` key `titanbound.save.v1`.
- Added mobile joystick/touch controls and responsive UI.

## Work State
### Completed
- Project scaffolding, dependencies, and successful production build.
- `src/data.js`: types, 40+ moves, 19 species, 8 biomes, 8 gyms, treats, ingredients, XP/stats helpers.
- `src/art.js`: procedural creature models for 10 body archetypes, trainer model, nameplates, particles, glow sprites.
- `src/world.js`: per-region terrain, sky, props, gym structures, waystones, wild creatures, resource nodes, ambient particles, battle arenas.
- `src/stages.js`: animated title scene and trainer/starter selection stage.
- `src/style.css` + `index.html`: full title/creator/starter/world HUD/atlas/journal/crafting/battle UI.
- `src/audio.js`: procedural ambient chords and SFX.
- `src/battle.js`: turn engine, focus, statuses, enemy AI, capture, gym teams, level-ups, results.
- `src/main.js`: game loop, movement/camera, input, save/load, region travel, interactions, crafting, journal, HUD, minimap, gym dialogue, ending.
- Verified title, creator, and starter screens render in Chromium via Playwright.
- Fixed camera aspect bug by calling `this.resize()` in constructor.

### Active
- Visual QA and bug fixing of creator/starter framing and creature models.
- Need to inspect latest `/tmp/opencode/starter3.jpeg` after aspect-ratio fix.
- Need full end-to-end gameplay QA: begin journey, movement, wild battle, capture, crafting, gym battle, travel.

### Blocked
- PNG screenshots time out in Playwright; JPEG screenshots work (`--type=jpeg`).
- Three.js warns `PCFSoftShadowMap has been removed` and `THREE.Clock` deprecated; non-fatal.
- Favicon 404 is harmless.

## Next Move
1. Inspect `/tmp/opencode/starter3.jpeg`; confirm all three starters visible and framed.
2. Improve trainer visual design if needed (neck, coat/shoulders, face, camera composition).
3. Click Begin Journey, test world render, movement, interactions, and battle.
4. Run end-to-end checks for crafting, treat capture, gym win/badge, region travel, save/continue.
5. Fix runtime bugs and visual defects; re-run `npm run build`.
6. Remove or ignore `gallery.html` debug page before finalizing.
7. Test responsive/mobile layout.
8. Summarize assumptions and controls to user at completion.

## Relevant Files
- `src/main.js`: orchestrator, UI state, movement, save/load, interactions, modals, HUD/minimap.
- `src/battle.js`: combat engine and battle UI.
- `src/art.js`: creature/trainer procedural models and visual helpers.
- `src/world.js`: region generation, props, wild spawns, resources, battle arena.
- `src/data.js`: all game content/balance data.
- `src/stages.js`: title and character/starter 3D stages.
- `src/style.css`: complete visual design and responsive layout.
- `index.html`: screen/HUD/battle DOM and loaded fonts.
- `src/audio.js`: procedural audio.
- `gallery.html`: temporary creature inspection page; not linked.
- `package.json`: Vite/Three scripts and dependencies.
- `dist/`: built deployment output.

## Important Context
- Dev server runs in tmux session `titan` on `http://localhost:3002`.
- Playwright controls: `playwright-cli` browser is currently open; use `--type=jpeg` for screenshots.
- Title starts with buttons `#btn-new` and hidden `#btn-continue`; creator uses `#btn-to-partner`, starter uses `#btn-begin`.
- Debug handle: `window.__TITANBOUND__` exposes game instance; `window.__TITANBOUND__.mode`, `.stage`, `.world`, `.activeBattle`.
- `gallery.html` was created for creature inspection and is not part of game flow.
- Latest verified screenshots: `/tmp/opencode/title.jpeg`, `/tmp/opencode/creator2.jpeg`, `/tmp/opencode/starter2.jpeg`; new `/tmp/opencode/starter3.jpeg` pending inspection.
- No git commit made; all work is uncommitted.

+/* ---------- painterly creature surfaces ----------
+   The creature art direction is lush, botanical watercolour rather than
+   hard neon low-poly.  These canvas maps give every body a mottled,
+   hand-painted wash and let the markings sit *in* the skin instead of
+   floating on top of it. */
+const skinCache = new Map()
+
+function hashString(str) {
+  let h = 2166136261
+  for (let i = 0; i < str.length; i++) { h ^= str.charCodeAt(i); h = Math.imul(h, 16777619) }
+  return h >>> 0
+}
+
+function rngFrom(seed) {
+  let a = seed
+  return () => {
+    a |= 0; a = a + 0x6D2B79F5 | 0
+    let t = Math.imul(a ^ a >>> 15, 1 | a)
+    t = t + Math.imul(t ^ t >>> 7, 61 | t) ^ t
+    return ((t ^ t >>> 14) >>> 0) / 4294967296
+  }
+}
+
+function paintWash(ctx, color, x, y, r, alpha) {
+  const g = ctx.createRadialGradient(x, y, 0, x, y, r)
+  g.addColorStop(0, color)
+  g.addColorStop(0.55, color)
+  g.addColorStop(1, 'rgba(255,255,255,0)')
+  ctx.globalAlpha = alpha
+  ctx.fillStyle = g
+  ctx.beginPath(); ctx.arc(x, y, r, 0, Math.PI * 2); ctx.fill()
+  ctx.globalAlpha = 1
+}
+
+function skinTexture(art, kind = 'body') {
+  const base = kind === 'belly' ? art.belly : kind === 'mane' ? (art.mane || art.belly) : kind === 'accent' ? art.accent : art.body
+  const key = `${art.body}|${art.belly}|${art.accent}|${art.glow}|${art.pattern}|${kind}`
+  if (skinCache.has(key)) return skinCache.get(key)
+  const canvas = document.createElement('canvas')
+  canvas.width = 256; canvas.height = 256
+  const ctx = canvas.getContext('2d')
+  const rnd = rngFrom(hashString(key))
+  ctx.fillStyle = base
+  ctx.fillRect(0, 0, 256, 256)
+
+  // Broad translucent watercolour blooms.
+  const bloomColors = kind === 'belly'
+    ? [art.body, art.belly, art.accent, '#fffdf4']
+    : [art.belly, art.accent, art.glow, art.body, '#fffdf4']
+  for (let i = 0; i < 30; i++) {
+    paintWash(ctx, bloomColors[Math.floor(rnd() * bloomColors.length)], rnd() * 256, rnd() * 256, 18 + rnd() * 72, 0.045 + rnd() * 0.07)
+  }
+
+  // Organic pigment speckles and tiny leaf-vein arcs.
+  for (let i = 0; i < 170; i++) {
+    ctx.globalAlpha = 0.06 + rnd() * 0.15
+    ctx.fillStyle = rnd() > 0.52 ? art.accent : art.belly
+    const s = 0.6 + rnd() * 2.2
+    ctx.beginPath(); ctx.ellipse(rnd() * 256, rnd() * 256, s, s * (0.5 + rnd()), rnd() * 3, 0, Math.PI * 2); ctx.fill()
+  }
+  ctx.globalAlpha = 1
+
+  if (kind === 'body') {
+    const mark = art.pattern
+    if (mark === 'stripes') {
+      ctx.strokeStyle = art.belly
+      ctx.globalAlpha = 0.32
+      ctx.lineWidth = 9 + rnd() * 5
+      for (let i = 0; i < 8; i++) {
+        ctx.beginPath()
+        const x = 8 + i * 33 + rnd() * 6
+        ctx.moveTo(x, -20)
+        ctx.bezierCurveTo(x + 18, 55, x - 18, 150, x + 12, 276)
+        ctx.stroke()
+      }
+    } else if (mark === 'spots') {
+      ctx.fillStyle = art.belly
+      for (let i = 0; i < 24; i++) {
+        ctx.globalAlpha = 0.28 + rnd() * 0.25
+        const r = 3 + rnd() * 9
+        ctx.beginPath(); ctx.arc(rnd() * 256, rnd() * 256, r, 0, Math.PI * 2); ctx.fill()
+      }
+    } else if (mark === 'rings' || mark === 'shell') {
+      ctx.strokeStyle = art.accent
+      ctx.globalAlpha = 0.25
+      ctx.lineWidth = 4
+      for (let i = 0; i < 10; i++) {
+        ctx.beginPath(); ctx.ellipse(rnd() * 256, rnd() * 256, 10 + rnd() * 34, 8 + rnd() * 26, rnd() * 3, 0, Math.PI * 2); ctx.stroke()
+      }
+    } else if (mark === 'lava' || mark === 'glow' || mark === 'constellation') {
+      ctx.strokeStyle = art.glow
+      ctx.globalAlpha = 0.42
+      ctx.lineWidth = 2
+      for (let i = 0; i < 9; i++) {
+        ctx.beginPath()
+        let x = rnd() * 256, y = rnd() * 256
+        ctx.moveTo(x, y)
+        for (let j = 0; j < 4; j++) { x += (rnd() - 0.5) * 55; y += (rnd() - 0.5) * 55; ctx.lineTo(x, y) }
+        ctx.stroke()
+      }
+    } else if (mark === 'moss' || mark === 'snow') {
+      ctx.fillStyle = mark === 'snow' ? '#f7ffff' : '#6f9657'
+      for (let i = 0; i < 30; i++) {
+        ctx.globalAlpha = 0.22 + rnd() * 0.3
+        const r = 2 + rnd() * 7
+        ctx.beginPath(); ctx.ellipse(rnd() * 256, rnd() * 256, r, r * 0.7, rnd() * 3, 0, Math.PI * 2); ctx.fill()
+      }
+    }
+    ctx.globalAlpha = 1
+  }
+
+  // Soft vertical light, like a wash of sun through leaves.
+  const light = ctx.createLinearGradient(0, 0, 0, 256)
+  light.addColorStop(0, 'rgba(255,250,220,0.14)')
+  light.addColorStop(0.45, 'rgba(255,255,255,0)')
+  light.addColorStop(1, 'rgba(20,45,32,0.10)')
+  ctx.fillStyle = light
+  ctx.fillRect(0, 0, 256, 256)
+
+  const tex = new THREE.CanvasTexture(canvas)
+  tex.colorSpace = THREE.SRGBColorSpace
+  tex.wrapS = tex.wrapT = THREE.RepeatWrapping
+  tex.anisotropy = 4
+  skinCache.set(key, tex)
+  return tex
+}
+
+function organicMaterial(art, kind = 'body', opts = {}) {
+  const base = kind === 'belly' ? art.belly : kind === 'mane' ? (art.mane || art.belly) : kind === 'accent' ? art.accent : kind === 'wing' ? (art.wings || art.accent) : art.body
+  const m = material('#ffffff', {
+    roughness: opts.roughness ?? 0.8,
+    metalness: 0,
+    flatShading: false,
+    transparent: opts.transparent,
+    opacity: opts.opacity,
+    side: opts.side,
+    emissive: opts.emissive || art.glow,
+    emissiveIntensity: opts.emissiveIntensity ?? 0.035
+  })
+  m.map = skinTexture(art, kind)
+  m.color.set('#ffffff')
+  m.needsUpdate = true
+  return m
+}
+
+function leafGeometry(length = 0.5, width = 0.2) {
+  const shape = new THREE.Shape()
+  shape.moveTo(0, 0)
+  shape.bezierCurveTo(-width, length * 0.22, -width * 0.9, length * 0.72, 0, length)
+  shape.bezierCurveTo(width * 0.9, length * 0.72, width, length * 0.22, 0, 0)
+  return new THREE.ShapeGeometry(shape, 8)
+}
+
+function addLeafSpray(parent, art, opts = {}) {
+  const group = new THREE.Group()
+  const count = opts.count ?? 6
+  const leafMat = organicMaterial(art, opts.kind || 'accent', { side: THREE.DoubleSide, roughness: 0.85 })
+  const rnd = rngFrom(hashString(`${art.body}-${opts.seed || 1}`))
+  for (let i = 0; i < count; i++) {
+    const leaf = new THREE.Mesh(leafGeometry((opts.length || 0.46) * (0.75 + rnd() * 0.5), (opts.width || 0.2) * (0.75 + rnd() * 0.45)), leafMat)
+    const a = (i / count) * Math.PI * 2 + rnd() * 0.4
+    const r = opts.radius ?? 0.62
+    leaf.position.set(Math.cos(a) * r, rnd() * 0.18, Math.sin(a) * r)
+    leaf.rotation.set(-0.3 + rnd() * 0.6, a + Math.PI / 2, (rnd() - 0.5) * 0.5)
+    leaf.castShadow = true
+    group.add(leaf)
+  }
+  group.position.copy(opts.position || new V(0, 0, 0))
+  group.rotation.copy(opts.rotation || new THREE.Euler())
+  parent.add(group)
+  return group
+}
+

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Build a complete, playable 3D creature collector adventure in Three.js with 8 regions, gyms, leveling, battles, crafting, trainer customization, and original monster-sized creatures.
- Shift the visual direction toward the supplied reference: lush watercolor/botanical creature illustrations with organic forms, expressive faces, leaf-like details, varied natural patterns, and vivid but soft colors.

## Requirements
- 8 explorable regions and competitive gyms.
- Fun leveling system.
- Capture via battling and treats crafted from scavenged materials.
- Male/female trainer customization.
- Original creature designs, Monster Hunter-sized but can be cute.
- Turn-based Pokémon-style battles.
- Build immediately without clarifying questions; note assumptions only at completion.
- Newer requirement: art style should resemble the provided watercolor creature sheet, not the earlier neon low-poly direction.
- Preserve procedural asset approach; no external art assets.

## Decisions
- Vite + Three.js with procedural geometry and canvas textures.
- Title `TITANBOUND`, 8 themed regions, 19 creatures, 8 gym leaders/sigils.
- Real-time third-person exploration plus separate turn-based battle arena.
- Progress stored in `localStorage` under `titanbound.save.v1`.
- Mobile joystick/touch controls and responsive UI.
- Art pivot: painterly canvas skin textures, smooth organic surfaces, leaf frills/antlers, larger expressive eyes, botanical world understory, and reduced neon bloom/lighting.

## Work State
### Completed
- Project scaffolding, dependencies, successful production builds.
- `src/data.js`: types, 40+ moves, 19 species, 8 biomes, 8 gyms, treats, ingredients, XP/stat helpers.
- `src/art.js`: procedural creature/trainer models, effects, nameplates; now partially reworked toward painterly organic art.
- `src/world.js`: region terrain, props, gyms, waystones, wild creatures, resources, particles, battle arenas.
- `src/stages.js`: animated title scene and trainer/starter selection stage.
- `src/main.js`: game loop, movement/camera, input, save/load, travel, interactions, crafting, journal, HUD, gym dialogue, ending.
- `src/battle.js`: turn engine, focus, statuses, AI, capture, gym teams, level-ups, results.
- Fixed runtime crash in `Game.updatePlayer` caused by undefined `t`.
- Verified world rendering, wild encounter, treat capture, crafting, gym battle/badge, atlas travel, and save/continue.
- Added canvas watercolor skin maps and `organicMaterial`; replaced faceted body geometry with smooth spheres; enlarged eyes with catchlights.
- Added leaf sprays to bodies, tails, heads, antlers, drake/bird necks; reduced Ripplefin ring glow; added Ripplefin fins/cheek fins.
- Added 92 broadleaf understory plants with blossoms to world generation.
- Reduced renderer exposure/bloom and battle-arena lighting.

### Active
- Final visual QA of the new painterly art direction after the latest `art.js` and `world.js` edits.
- Need to rerun `npm run build`; the last build predates antler foliage, texture contrast, Ripplefin fins, and bloom/lighting changes.
- Need to inspect latest starter/battle/world screenshots and tune creature colors, pattern visibility, and foliage density.
- Mobile battle flow still needs testing; earlier mobile attempt did not actually start a battle because `interact()` ran before `nearest` updated.

### Blocked
- PNG screenshots time out in Playwright; JPEG works (`--type=jpeg`).
- Three.js warnings: `THREE.Clock` deprecated and `PCFSoftShadowMap has been removed`; non-fatal.
- Favicon 404 harmless.
- Known mobile HUD overlap: `.hud-center` at `top: 78px; left: 12px` covers the objective; party dock overlaps joystick with larger parties.

## Next Move
1. Rerun `npm run build` after the latest art edits.
2. Reload browser, clear storage if needed, and inspect new starter/title/world/battle screenshots.
3. Tune creature palette/pattern contrast and leaf density; verify all three starters read clearly against cards.
4. Fix mobile CSS: move badge rack below objective, reposition party dock above the joystick, adjust interact prompt spacing.
5. Test mobile world controls, battle layout, attack, capture, and journal.
6. Run full desktop regression: new game → starter → movement → gather → craft → capture → gym → atlas travel → reload/continue.
7. Remove or ignore `gallery.html`; finalize with controls and assumptions summary.
8. Keep all changes uncommitted unless a commit is explicitly requested.

## Relevant Files
- `src/art.js`: procedural creature/trainer art, painterly textures, organic materials, leaf details.
- `src/world.js`: terrain, biomes, props, broadleaf flora, waystones, gyms, battle arenas.
- `src/main.js`: orchestration, UI, movement, save/load, interactions, HUD, modals.
- `src/battle.js`: combat engine and battle UI.
- `src/stages.js`: title, creator, and starter 3D scenes.
- `src/style.css`: all UI styling and responsive layout; mobile overlap fixes pending.
- `src/data.js`: species, moves, regions, gyms, treats, ingredients, palettes.
- `index.html`: screens/HUD/battle DOM structure.
- `src/audio.js`: procedural audio/SFX.
- `gallery.html`: temporary creature inspection page, not part of game flow.
- `dist/`: built deployment output, currently stale relative to latest edits.

## Important Context
- Dev server runs at `http://localhost:3002`.
